bugs.title: New mission creation vs dispatching work into an existing mission is unclear
Orca/Windows notifications expose raw internal run IDs and are noisy

RESCOPED 2026-09-03 (ledger correction, see BUG-08 vs BUG-17 note below): negated consequential language (e.g. "do not merge/push/deploy") must classify as a restriction, never a request -- classification correctness only. The original title's second half ("...may fail to consume explicit approval once") is now BUG-17 -- a distinct, still-REPORTED, not-yet-started mechanism. This entry's READY_FOR_ADOPTION applies ONLY to the classification-correctness scope below, never to approval-consumption, which does not exist and was never implemented under this id.
evidence: LEDGER CORRECTION (2026-09-03, prompted by an explicit operator check): this bug's original title bundled two materially different things -- (a) negated language must classify as a restriction (a pure classification-correctness question, real bugs found/fixed/verified below) and (b) a scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism (a distinct, unbuilt feature -- see the 'SCOPING DECISION' entry below, which was already honest about it being deferred and not started). Marking the WHOLE bug READY_FOR_ADOPTION was status inflation given ACCEPT-07's acceptance criterion ('...consumes scoped approval once') was never satisfied. Split: this id now covers ONLY (a), genuinely done and 3x independently verified below; (b) is split out to BUG-17, status REPORTED, not started. ACCEPT-07 stays REPORTED until BUG-17 lands too -- see its own entry in the acceptance[] array below.

Independent read-only investigation (separate agent context) traced the actual regex logic live against real messages: every example the ledger's own evidence named ("do not merge this", "please do not push to production", a negation-plus-unrelated-directive combined message) already classified correctly -- the adversarial-hardened comma/"but"/em-dash clause-splitting genuinely works.

But it found a REAL, reproducible gap in the same class: splitIntoClauses (chat-responder.mjs) never treated a bare "and" (no comma) as a clause boundary, so a negation and a genuine, separate directive joined only by "and" stayed one clause and the negation laundered the directive through as non-TIM_REQUIRED. Live-reproduced: 'do not deploy this and push it now' -> AUTO_DECIDE (wrong); 'please do not deploy and go ahead and merge this' -> RECOMMEND_AND_PROCEED (wrong). Reproduces identically on the Command surface (command-responder.mjs reuses the same functions unmodified).

Fix: added \band\b to the same clause-boundary normalization regex, exactly mirroring the existing "but"/comma/em-dash precedent. Both repro cases now correctly TIM_REQUIRED; verified live and via 4 new regression tests (chat-responder.test.mjs) plus the full existing 25-case suite unchanged (34/34 total across chat+command responder tests).

Investigation also found: there is NO approval-consumption mechanism anywhere in the codebase (grepped server/domain for approve/consume/grant/scope) -- every chat/command turn is independently reclassified from the bare current message with zero conversational memory. Practically this makes TIM_REQUIRED for push/merge/deploy/publish/credentials/money/adopt an unconditional refusal via chat today: restating with the keyword re-triggers TIM_REQUIRED every time, and chat is structurally zero-tool (--tools "") plus chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's generated plans hard-forbid this action class regardless -- so there is currently no execution path for this class of action via chat at all, whatever the approval state. respondTimRequired()'s old text falsely promised a 'tell me explicitly to proceed and I'll surface exactly what would change... before anything happens' preview flow that doesn't exist anywhere -- fixed to honestly say chat cannot act on it and point to the real surface (Adoption tab / terminal).

SCOPING DECISION: a genuine scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism (the user's fuller ask: 'consumed once', 'must not leak to another operation/project/action class') is real product value but is itself a security-sensitive, non-trivial feature (new persisted state, new UI, cross-turn tracking) -- deliberately deferred to a following bounded wave rather than rushed in alongside this wave's other 5 bugs, per the mission driver's own explicit allowance ('this stabilization wave or the immediately following bounded wave'). What's fixed now (the real negation gap, and the honesty fix removing the false promise/refusal-loop) is real, verified, and independently investigated; the deferred piece is disclosed here, not silently dropped.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (first pass) found the \band\b fix itself introduced a NEW real false-negative regression: when 'and'-splitting isolates an informal, subject-less future-tense fragment as its own clause (e.g. '...and will deploy after that', '...and should merge soon'), that clause starts with a bare inquiry-opener word ('will'/'should') purely by grammatical coincidence -- INQUIRY_OPENERS' bare-opener alternative wrongly read it as a question with no '?' anywhere. Live-reproduced: 'run the tests and will deploy after that' -> AUTO_DECIDE (wrong, was TIM_REQUIRED-worthy).

Fixed: split INQUIRY_OPENERS into BARE_OPENER (bare opener word) and TELL_ME_WHETHER (the 'tell me...whether' shape, unconditional). BARE_OPENER now additionally requires the clause's own SENTENCE to contain a real '?' -- TELL_ME_WHETHER stays unconditional since it's unambiguously interrogative regardless of punctuation. Verified against both the new regression cases (now correctly TIM_REQUIRED) and every prior passing case (unchanged) live before adding tests. 2 new regression tests added (31/31 chat-responder tests pass).

Second independent-verification pass confirmed both the negation-gap fix and its own found BARE_OPENER regression are correct (READY) via ~20 adversarial phrasings the implementer never tried, plus its own sentence-vs-clause scoping check. It also found a THIRD real, pre-existing gap (unrelated to the 'and' fix, surfaced incidentally while re-checking it): PROHIBITION_MARKERS' bare 'not'/'no' match had no idiom awareness, so 'whether ... or not'/'no matter' (meaning 'regardless') wrongly read as real negations -- 'deploy it whether tim likes it or not' classified AUTO_DECIDE instead of TIM_REQUIRED.

Fixed: IDIOMATIC_NON_NEGATION strips these two idioms from the clause before the PROHIBITION_MARKERS test (never a separate branch, so a clause whose ONLY negation-looking text is one of these idioms falls through correctly, while a real 'do not X, no matter what anyone says' still correctly reads as negated on its own 'do not' text). 3 new regression tests; 33/33 chat-responder tests, 56/56 across the full chat/command surface pass.

Third independent-verification pass: READY. Adversarially tested 14 more idiom variants (capitalization, verbs, comma placement, 'and'-joined) -- no remaining false-negative found -- and confirmed structurally the fix can only ever push classification toward the safe TIM_REQUIRED branch, never away from it (stripping a substring can only make a clause read as MORE of a genuine directive). 38/38 chat/command tests pass. Final full-suite sanity check on the whole wave: tsf/ 994 tests, 992 pass, 1 fail (keep-going-autonomy-proof.test.mjs, the documented pre-existing Windows-contention flake, reconfirmed passing in isolation twice), 1 skipped; tsf/ui/ typecheck clean, build clean, 46/46 tests pass.

All three rounds of independent verification (separate agent context each time, per HQ.md's provider-split rule) are clean. The deferred scoped-approval-consumption mechanism is still NOT started and NOT claimed done -- disclosed as a following-wave item, not silently dropped.

LIVE-VERIFIED: started a real Keep Going run on the safe local FIXTURE project in the real running app, confirmed the CONTINUE badge showed while ACTIVE, then Paused it and confirmed the badge correctly disappeared (Gap analysis text stayed, the misleading pill did not) -- screenshotted before/after.

bugs.title: Planner Chat can be blind to durable state visible in Keep Going / Flight Recorder
evidence: Reproduced and root-caused precisely: chat-responder.mjs's LIVE_RUN_INTENTS grounds only STATUS/NEXT_ACTION/FINISHED in the live run; live-planner.mjs's buildProjectContextCapsule (used for every other phrasing, whenever a live LLM provider is configured) never read opState.keepGoingRuns at all -- http-server.mjs's own comment already disclosed this ('the live conversational planner call below has zero awareness of Keep Going state').

Fix (single source of truth, matches BUG-14's theme): domain/live-work-feed.mjs's new describeLiveRunStatus(run, gap) is the one grounding sentence now reused by both call sites. chat-responder.mjs's respond() appends a liveRunFooter for every non-terminal-run intent that previously ignored the run entirely (HEALTH/ADOPTION/RATIONALE/GENERAL/CRITIQUE/FIX_REQUEST/RESEARCH/DISPATCH_REQUEST). live-planner.mjs's buildProjectContextCapsule gained an optional live_run_status field, computed by invokeLivePlanner from the same opState.keepGoingRuns/compareStateToGoal http-server.mjs's statusWorthy check already uses; contracts/project-context-capsule.schema.v1.json updated to match.

34/34 chat/command-responder tests, 23/23 live-planner tests (incl. 2 new capsule unit tests + 1 new end-to-end invokeLivePlanner proof through the real stub-CLI transmitted system prompt), 18/18 live-work-feed tests (incl. 3 new describeLiveRunStatus tests), 7/7 planner-eval-runner tests all pass -- zero regressions.

LIVE-VERIFIED with a REAL live provider call (not the stub): asked Planner Chat 'is it healthy?' (a HEALTH-intent question, previously blind to any run) against a project with a real paused Keep Going run -- the real Claude Code/Sonnet 5 planner response correctly said 'there's a candidate in READY_FOR_ADOPTION state waiting on your decision (the Keep Going run is paused on it)', proving live_run_status actually reached and was used by a genuine live LLM call end to end, and cross-checked the same run's state against Flight Recorder's timeline in the same session -- all three surfaces agreed.

INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (separate agent context, adversarial review + own test run): READY. Confirmed liveRunFooter is applied only in the final RESPONDERS[intent](project) fallback branch of respond() -- never on TIM_REQUIRED or the dispatch-worthy/statusWorthy branches -- and confirmed invokeLivePlanner's liveRun/liveGap computation is null-safe for a project with no run or a missing keepGoingRuns key.

bugs.title: No trustworthy persistent global surface showing RUNNING / PAUSED / WAITING / STALLED / VERIFYING / NEEDS YOU / READY FOR ADOPTION
evidence: Investigated thoroughly first (background architecture-mapping pass across all 7 surfaces): the domain layer already had a genuine, real single source of truth (domain/live-work-feed.mjs's projectLiveWorkFeedState + domain/fleet-work-status.mjs's fleetWorkStatus, already shared by Work and Command). The real bug was that not every surface consumed it uniformly -- fixed each confirmed gap:

(1) HomePage.tsx silently dropped work.needsYou/work.stalled from its Needs You bucket and showed stale mission.state text instead of the run's real liveWorkFeed.reason (WorkPage.tsx already did this correctly) -- fixed, both now match Work's own logic.

(2) FleetPage.tsx never called /api/work at all -- zero run-state vocabulary reached Fleet Planning. Fixed via new ui/src/lib/work-feed-lookup.ts (buildLiveWorkFeedLookup/liveWorkFeedBadgeVariant, reused wherever a live state needs a badge), wired into FleetPage's Work Set rows.

(3) Real drift found between the domain projection and its client-side mirror (ui/src/lib/live-work-feed.ts): domain has an inFlightWave-still-set-but-last-checkpointed-WAVE_STALLED STALLED override the client had no equivalent for. Fixed by exposing a new inFlightWaveStalled boolean on the server view (keep-going-controller.mjs, same 'expose exactly the boolean' pattern as the existing dispatchTickActive), consumed by the client mirror.

No dedicated always-visible global chrome indicator was built this wave (SystemStatusIndicator.tsx is confirmed to be about runtime/update identity, not mission state, and building a new persistent header/sidebar element is a larger, separate UI addition) -- disclosed as a real remaining gap, not claimed done.

LIVE-VERIFIED (not just unit-tested): ran the real standalone server + built UI in a real Chrome tab, started a real Keep Going run on the safe local FIXTURE project, and confirmed Keep Going/Flight Recorder/Planner Chat all showed the exact same real run consistently across all three surfaces (paused state, same checkpoints, same timeline) with zero console errors.
10/10 keep-going-controller tests, 17/17 live-work-feed-ui tests, 5/5 work-feed-lookup tests, tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean -- zero regressions.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (first pass) found a real defect: HomePage.tsx's combined needsYou array used a bare key={p.id}, but work.blocked (a legacy, run-independent classification) can legitimately contain the SAME project id as work.needsYou/stalled (a BLOCKED-mission project can also have a live NEEDS_YOU run) -- domain/work-feed-summary.mjs computes them independently -- a real React key collision, confirmed reproducible, that went untested (no HomePage.test.tsx existed).

Fixed: extracted the bucket-tagging into new ui/src/lib/home-needs-you-items.ts (buildHomeNeedsYouItems/homeNeedsYouItemKey), same key-prefix-per-bucket pattern WorkPage.tsx already uses for this identical overlap. 3 new unit tests directly reproduce the overlap case and assert distinct keys. HomePage.tsx now uses this tested module instead of inline untested logic. tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean, 46/46 ui tests pass.

Second independent-verification pass: READY. Confirmed the key-prefix tagging produces distinct keys for the real overlap case, confirmed HomePage.tsx correctly uses the new tested module (no remaining inline broken version), 3/3 home-needs-you-items tests + full ui typecheck/build clean.
The persistent global indicator remains a disclosed gap for a following wave.

bugs.title: Stalled-run recovery lacks clear reason, heartbeat, worker/provider, retries, and Resume / Retry / Replan / Abandon actions
evidence: keep-going-tsf-orca-1787691592122 could not be located on disk in this session (searched every worktree's .local-state for the run id/projectId -- zero matches, likely only ever existed in a live process's persisted state not present in any checked-out worktree here). A future wave needing it should fetch GET /api/keep-going/tsf-orca live against whatever process actually serves it, not search the filesystem.

Ground-truth investigation (read-only, ahead of implementation) precisely separated what's real vs. would be fabricated for this bug's own ask: REASON -- real (silentForMs since inFlightWave.dispatchedAt, checkpoint note 'silent for <ms>ms', two real evidence arrays: dispatchIds on the STALLED transition, taskIds on the WAVE_STALLED checkpoint) but not yet exposed to the UI beyond the raw ms note. HEARTBEAT -- no true per-worker heartbeat exists anywhere (orca-runtime.mjs's mapOrchestrationFacts always emits lastHeartbeatAt:null, a disclosed limitation; domain/keep-going.mjs's detectStall exists but is never called for exactly this reason) -- inFlightWave.dispatchedAt + silentForMs is the honest substitute, never a literal 'last heartbeat at' claim. WORKER/PROVIDER -- genuinely not persisted anywhere on a dispatch record (only taskId/dispatchId/workItemId/scope are); keep-going-controller.mjs's workers:[] is still correctly, honestly hardcoded empty -- any agent/provider/model label would be fabricated without a new live Orca task-show/worker-show lookup keyed by the real taskId. RETRIES -- already real and already correctly displayed, nothing to fix. ACTIONS -- Abandon is real, wired end-to-end, and (per keep-going-controller.mjs's abandon handler) already auto-resumes the run afterward -- so the bug's separate 'Resume' ask may be based on a misunderstanding: a bare Resume button on STALLED (real domain primitive, real route, RUN_ALLOWED permits it) would NOT actually clear the stuck inFlightWave and would likely just have the run re-stall on the next tick, so exposing it as its own control needs care, not just a UI toggle. 'Retry' (a single stalled work item, not the whole wave) has NO domain primitive anywhere. 'Replan' has NO domain primitive anywhere at all -- the word only appears in descriptive UI copy, never a callable function.

Implication for a following wave: an honest BUG-15 fix is smaller than the bug's literal wording implies -- surface the real stalled-since duration/taskIds/workItemIds/scope, clarify that Abandon already includes resume, and explicitly do NOT add fabricated worker/provider labels or Retry/Replan buttons with no real backing primitive (those would need real new domain work first, disclosed here rather than faked).

bugs.title: Investigate: Flight Recorder records waves while Evidence shows no recorded results
evidence: Confirmed as a real data-integrity gap, root-caused: Flight Recorder (flight-recorder-http-routes.mjs) reads real run.waves via buildRunTimeline; Evidence (ProjectDetailPage.tsx) reads project.evidence.resultCapsules, which onboarded-project-projection.mjs hardcoded to [] with zero write path from a settled wave -- true for every real onboarded project.

Fix: domain/keep-going-result-capsules.mjs's resultCapsulesFromRun(run) -- a pure projection over the SAME run.waves Flight Recorder already reads (never a second, independently-drifting store), honestly deriving only fields the real dispatch/settle path actually records (id/status/workerIdentity.orcaSessionId; filesChanged/testsRun left empty, never fabricated). Wired through onboarded-project-projection.mjs's new optional `run` param and project-catalog.mjs's opState.keepGoingRuns lookup.
9/9 new unit tests pass across domain (keep-going-result-capsules.test.mjs) and projection-wiring (onboarded-project-projection.test.mjs) layers.

Live-verified only that the Evidence/Flight Recorder tabs render without crashing against a real running run (the FIXTURE project used for that live pass has its own separate, unrelated resultCapsules source -- fixture-project.mjs -- so it does not exercise this specific fix; the fix itself only applies to real onboarded projects, proven at the projection layer by the unit tests above, not yet observed live against a real onboarded project with a real run in this session).

INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (separate agent context): READY, with an optional non-blocking hardening suggestion (resultCapsulesFromRun didn't guard a missing run.waves field or a non-array waveResult.outcomes -- neither reachable via any real write path today, but defense-in-depth). Applied: run.waves ?? [] guard + Array.isArray(outcomes) check, 2 new tests covering both shapes. 7/7 keep-going-result-capsules tests pass.

bugs.title: Planner Chat/Command has no scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism for a TIM_REQUIRED (consequential) action -- split out of BUG-08 2026-09-03 as its own tracked item (see BUG-08's own title/evidence for why)
evidence: Split from BUG-08 during ledger reconciliation: BUG-08's classification-correctness half (negated language must never read as a request) is genuinely done and independently verified; this half -- 'explicit scoped approval must be consumed once,' 'must not leak to another operation/project/action class,' 'Planner Chat must not repeatedly ask for the same authorization after the exact requested action has already been approved' (the mission driver's own wording) -- is NOT started. Nothing under this id has been implemented.

Ground truth already established while investigating BUG-08 (real, not assumed): there is NO approval-consumption mechanism anywhere in the codebase (grepped server/domain for approve/consume/grant/scope -- only unrelated hits: domain/operator-action-lifecycle.mjs's separate Adoption-surface approve-adoption/approve-local-commit, and a cosmetic 'approvals' evidence list in live-planner.mjs). Every chat/command turn is independently reclassified from the bare current message with zero conversational memory (chat-responder.mjs's classifyDecision, command-responder.mjs -- both fresh per call, no history threaded in for authorization purposes).

Also already established: chat is structurally zero-tool (--tools "", live-planner.mjs) and chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's generated plans hard-forbid push/merge/deploy/publish/credentials/money/adoption regardless of any approval state -- so for THOSE specific action classes there is currently no execution path via chat at all, whatever gets 'approved.' The one action class where a real approval-consumption mechanism would have actual teeth is the Adoption surface's own approve-adoption/approve-local-commit primitives (domain/operator-action-lifecycle.mjs) -- a future implementation should scope to what can actually execute, not fabricate a generic mechanism for actions chat can't perform anyway.

respondTimRequired()'s text was already corrected (as part of BUG-08) to stop promising a reconfirm/preview flow that didn't exist -- that dishonesty is fixed regardless of whether this bug is picked up.

SCOPING NOTE for implementation: a real mechanism needs persisted, scoped state (which exact action, which project, requested-at, expires-at), a single-use consume-on-match check, and must not silently expand scope (a 'yes' approving one push must never be read as approving a later, different deploy). This is genuinely security-sensitive -- deserves its own reproduction/design pass, not a rushed bolt-on alongside unrelated work.
Not started. No reproduction, no fix, no tests, no verification yet.
